As more data are acquired, it might become possible to detect the strong lensing signature of dwarf galaxy satellites, and to find lenses with an unusually large number of images. In this paper, we try to anticipate the kind of discoveries that these data will bring along.

papers.title: Large dust grains escaping from a supernova remnant
papers.abstract: Dust grains produced in the supernova (SN) ejecta at early ages are partially destroyed in hot gas of the SN remnant. Large grains owing to their inertia can overtake the forward shock front of the remnant and move through the ambient interstellar medium. Using one-dimensional gas dynamics including the dust destruction we study the transport of dust grains inside the SN remnant and the ambient medium. Here we estimate the surviving and escaping mass fractions depending on the cut-off (maximum) size in a power-law distribution of grain sizes. We found that these fractions follow closely each other at late age of the SN remnant, i.e. almost all grains, which have survived in the remnant, leave it for the ambient interstellar medium. At the age of 30 kyr -- the onset of the radiative phase with density $n\sim 1$ cm$^{-3}$ with solar metallicity -- the escaping/surviving mass fractions for the cut-off size of several microns reach about $0.7-0.8$. The major part of these grains have size larger than $1~μ$m and initially located at distances $\gtrsim 0.2$ of the ejecta core radius. Later dust grains at velocity of several hundreds km/s escaping the remnant continue to be destroyed due to kinetic sputtering in the interstellar medium. Grains with sizes of several microns are destroyed marginally and therefore will survive in the interstellar gas. After decelerating of grains in the medium the surviving mass fraction of grains produced in the SN remnant, which evolves in an ambient gas with $n$ from 1 to 100 cm$^{-3}$, is from $\sim 0.5$ to $\sim 0.3$, respectively, for the cut-off grain size $a_{cut} = 10~μ$m. A decrease of the cut-off size in the distribution results in lower surviving mass fraction.

papers.title: Correlation of galactic very-high-energy gamma-ray sources detected by LHAASO with high-energy neutrinos
papers.abstract: We conducted an investigation into the possible correlation between very-high-energy (VHE, $E>$ 0.1 TeV) gamma-ray sources, as identified by the Large High Altitude Air Shower Observatory (LHAASO), and high-energy neutrino events captured by the IceCube Neutrino Observatory. For this analysis, we utilized the First LHAASO catalog, which comprises 90 VHE gamma-ray sources, and the IceCube Event Catalog of Alert Tracks (IceCat-1), which includes 348 track-like neutrino events. Through Monte Carlo simulations, we assessed the correlations between the neutrino events and LHAASO sources, achieving the best p-values of 0.237, 0.312, and 0.115, respectively, for all LHAASO sources, KM2A sources, and WCDA sources. These findings imply that the spatial coincidence between LHAASO sources and neutrino alerts is relatively weak. Furthermore, under the assumption that gamma-rays are exclusively generated through hadronic interactions, we estimated the most optimistic theoretical neutrino fluxes from LHAASO sources and compared them with the IceCube observed fluxes. The results indicate that the majority of these sources are improbable counterparts to the detected neutrinos. In conclusion, LHAASO sources could be potential galactic neutrino emitters but currently do not exhibit compelling evidence, thereby underscoring the necessity for elevated sensitivity levels in forthcoming detection instruments like IceCube-Gen2.

papers.title: Development and characterization of a millimeter-wave circular polarization observation method using a quarter-wave plate with Simons Array
papers.abstract: We have developed and demonstrated a method for measuring circular polarization at 90 GHz by combining a quarter-wave plate (QWP) and a continuously rotating half-wave plate (HWP). While many bolometric experiments at millimeter wavelengths focus on measuring linear polarization, observations of circular polarization in millimeter waves may open a new window into astrophysics and cosmology. We present a novel approach to circular-polarization search using linear-polarization-sensitive detectors by incorporating a QWP in the optics. The Simons Array was originally designed for precise linear polarization measurements, and we subsequently installed a QWP in front of the receiver targeting 90 GHz. The QWP converts incident circular polarization to linear polarization, allowing detection with our detectors. Laboratory measurements demonstrate a QWP conversion efficiency of 99.0%. We apply our method to observations of unpolarized and linearly polarized bright sources, Jupiter and Tau A. Using these observations, we establish the calibration and characterize the instrumental leakages relevant to circular polarization measurements. The measured polarization efficiency adopted for Stokes $V$ is $46\pm2$%, and the measured U-to-V leakage is $-11.7\pm5.1$%. We measure a circular polarization fraction of $V/I=0.78\pm0.42$% for Tau A, showing no significant detection and providing a consistency check of the calibration and systematic-uncertainty treatment. These results establish the instrument response model and calibration parameters used for the companion circular-polarization source search.

papers.title: Optimal Design of Shaped Pupil Lyot Coronagraph for China's Large Segmented Telescope
papers.abstract: China's next-generation large telescopes, such as the Expandable Aperture Segmented Telescope (EAST) and the Large Optical/Infrared Telescope (LOT), are being planned as flagship facilities for high-angular-resolution astronomy, including the direct imaging and characterization of exoplanetary systems (e.g., exoplanets, circumstellar disks). However, their segmented, centrally obscured apertures present significant challenges for coronagraph design: diffraction from segmented gaps and spiders severely limit contrast, particularly at small inner working angles (IWAs). To address this, we investigate an optimal Shaped Pupil Lyot Coronagraph (SPLC) architecture tailored for these telescopes, which combines a binary shaped pupil apodizer, a focal-plane occulting mask, and a Lyot stop to suppress stellar glare and enhance contrast. We further augment the coronagraph design with a two-deformable-mirror (2-DM) adaptive optics (AO) system to correct atmospheric turbulence and residual aberrations. End-to-end simulations based on site parameters for Lenghu in Qinghai Province and assuming idealized extreme AO (ExAO) correction demonstrate that the optimized 2DM-SPLC designs can achieve raw contrasts of order 10^-6-10^-7 in the V, H, and K bands, providing an upper-bound estimate of the system performance. The simulated performance highlights the advantages of the SPLC in mitigating diffraction from segmented and centrally obscured pupils while maintaining a small IWA and practical throughput, indicating that the 2DM-SPLC is a promising coronagraphic architecture for high-contrast exoplanet imaging on China's future large segmented telescopes.

papers.title: Emergence of high-mass stars in complex fiber networks (EMERGE) VII. Multi-Tracer Column Density Synthesis
papers.abstract: Obtaining accurate estimates of the gas column density $\mathrm{N(H_2)}$ is crucial to determine the physical conditions of the molecular gas in the Interstellar Medium. This paper introduces the "Multi-Tracer Column Density Synthesis" (MT-CDS) technique, a new empirical approach to derive high dynamic-range column density maps with interferometers such as ALMA. We have compared the integrated intensity maps of two density selective tracers, namely HNC (1-0) and $\mathrm{N_2H^+}$ (1-0), obtained with IRAM-30m with ancillary Herschel column density estimates in seven star-forming regions in Orion and derived individual temperature-corrected conversion factors for each of these tracers. We applied these conversion factors obtained at low-resolution into similar high sensitivity ALMA observations to derive independent column density maps describing both the low $N_\mathrm{HNC}\mathrm{(H_2)}$ and high $N_\mathrm{N_2H^+}\mathrm{(H_2)}$ column density components at high spatial resolution (4.5"). We also combined these independent maps into estimates for the total gas column density gas $N_\mathrm{tot}\mathrm{(H_2)}$ sampling more than two orders of magnitude in column density between $\sim 10^{21.5}-10^{23.5}$ cm$^{-2}$. A comparison with independent ArTeMiS column density maps at intermediate resolution (8") shows typical deviations of $\lesssim$0.2 dex from our MT-CDS gas column density estimates. We obtained individual column density maps in five of our targets at $\sim$2000 au resolution in which ALMA observations were available, that is a factor of $\sim$5 better than originally calibrated. These results demonstrate the potential of this MT-CDS technique to retrieve accurate, high dynamic range $N\mathrm{(H_2)}$ total gas column density estimates at interferometric resolution combining multiple molecular line tracers.

papers.title: JWST observations of 47 Tucanae: I. The low-mass main sequence down to the hydrogen-burning limit
papers.abstract: We present the first results of a series of studies based on JWST observations of the globular cluster 47 Tucanae (47 Tuc, or NGC 104) obtained with NIRCam. By combining new data with earlier JWST observations, we derive high-precision proper motions (PMs) over a multi-year baseline (of ~3 years) and construct a clean sample of cluster members extending to very faint magnitudes (F444W~24.25 mag, corresponding to ~0.077 solar masses, slightly above the estimated hydrogen-burning limit of 47 Tuc, ~0.074 solar masses) along the main sequence (MS). We investigated the presence of the low-mass MS kink previously identified in 47 Tuc using the new F090W and F444W photometry. No significant signature of the feature is found using these filters, consistent with its proposed physical interpretation as a consequence of the transition in carbon chemistry toward a methane-dominated equilibrium in very low-mass stars. A comparison with theoretical isochrones indicates that the stellar population near the bottom of the MS is likely dominated by oxygen-poor stars, in agreement with previous findings. Using artificial-star tests, we quantify the completeness of our sample and show that the requirement of PM-based membership significantly limits the detection of the faintest objects, indicating that current JWST observations of 47 Tuc are not sufficiently deep to reliably trace the cluster's brown dwarf cooling sequence. The mass function (MF) of 47 Tuc shows a structured behaviour, with a break at ~0.15 solar masses not associated with the onset of convection, and a mild but systematic radial variation consistent with mass segregation. Our analysis indicates that the MF shape in this mass regime is more complex than a simple power-law description. This feature in the MF may point to a presently unrecognised mechanism affecting the formation or dynamical evolution of low-mass stars in globular clusters.

papers.title: A Nonlinear General Implicit Runge-Kutta Integrator for Multifluid Charged Dust and Gas
papers.abstract: Charged dust in magnetized gas is subject to aerodynamic drag and the Lorentz force, both of which can be difficult to model numerically in a fluid simulation where their characteristic timescales are shorter than the timestep set by the Courant condition. We present a two-stage general implicit Runge-Kutta (GIRK) source integrator for multifluid charged dust coupled to an ideal magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) gas, implemented in the open source GPU-accelerated quokka code. Drag and Lorentz forces are advanced together in one implicit source update, avoiding errors in the terminal drift that can arise when the two forces are advanced in separate substeps. The timestep is compared with a drag-Lorentz timescale to select between resolved and stiff branches. The resolved branch uses Gauss-Legendre coefficients, while the stiff branch uses a coefficient set designed to recover the terminal drift set by the drag-Lorentz balance. We also allow the dust stopping time and charge-to-mass ratio to depend on the evolving state, evaluating them separately at the two implicit stage states and solving the resulting nonlinear stage equations by Picard iteration. The source update conserves total gas-dust momentum, and its computational cost scales linearly with the number of dust species. Tests reproduce the expected drag damping and terminal drift, confirm the predicted gyromotion amplitude and phase errors, demonstrate accurate treatment of state-dependent source coefficients, and recover the expected wave, shock, and instability dynamics in dusty MHD flows.

papers.title: Spinformation: do gravitational-wave events carry information beyond effective spins?
papers.abstract: While the spin vectors of binary black holes offer insight into the astrophysical formation channels of these systems, individual spins are less precisely measured through gravitational-wave observations than the effective inspiral spin $χ_\mathrm{eff}$ and the effective precession spin $χ_\mathrm{p}$. Reducing to effective parameters discards information in the data, but how much information is lost has yet to be demonstrated. Here we show how to quantify whether individual mergers carry information about component spins beyond the constraints implied by effective parameters (a.k.a. spinformation) and apply the technique to GWTC-5. Thresholding on information loss $\gtrsim 0.25$ bits, over $80\%$ of gravitational-wave events in GWTC-5 have component spin posteriors described by $χ_\mathrm{eff}$ alone. Only $\sim3\%$ of gravitational-wave events have substantial spin information not explained by $χ_\mathrm{eff}$ and $χ_\mathrm{p}$. The catalog's component spin information is effectively two-dimensional in $χ_\mathrm{eff}$ and $χ_\mathrm{p}$. Using simulated signals, we find the noise realization can create or destroy over a bit of beyond-$χ_\mathrm{eff}$ information: the structure in real data may therefore be driven by noise. At current sensitivity, component spins provide interpretive\textemdash rather than informational\textemdash advantage over effective parameters.

papers.title: The Second Catalog of Low-Energy Fermi-LAT Sources
papers.abstract: We used 14 years of Fermi-Large Area Telescope (LAT) data to derive a catalog of sources detected between 20 MeV and 200 MeV. For each source we provide localization, spectral, and association information. The Second Catalog of Low-Energy Fermi-LAT sources (2FLE) contains 450 sources detected at $TS>25$, with median energy flux of $F_{20-200 \, \text{MeV}} = 1.9\times10^{-11}$ erg cm$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$. Using a Bayesian and likelihood-ratio method, we associate 377 2FLE sources with a known counterpart. Of the 325 objects associated with extragalactic sources, the dominant source class represented in the 2FLE are flat-spectrum radio quasars (FSRQ). Additionally, 52 sources are associated with Galactic sources. Three associated sources have not been previously detected in any $γ$-ray catalog and represent new $γ$-ray sources of known origin. We find that 387 2FLE sources have a positional cross-match with the 4FGL-DR4 sources. For the sources with a 4FGL counterpart, we compare the spectrum of the 2FLE source to the 4FGL spectral energy distributions. Of the 73 2FLE sources without multi-wavelength associations, 13 have a 4FGL counterpart that lacks classification, while 60 are newly discovered $γ$-ray sources. Among these 60 sources, 51 are found at high latitudes ($|b|>10^{\circ}$), and 38 are detected at $>10σ$. Additionally, we find that out of the 450 2FLE sources 45 are TeV emitters, and 6 are spatially coincident with a 1LHAASO source. The 2FLE helps us pave the way for reducing the ``MeV gap", and provides the most sensitive catalog between 20-200 MeV to date.

papers.title: Establishing baseline model performances for optical turbulence forecasting
papers.abstract: Accurate forecasting of optical turbulence (OT) is useful to optimise telescope scheduling and maximising observing efficiency, as the performance of adaptive optics systems strongly depends on turbulence conditions. While various numerical weather prediction and machine learning models are developed to predict these complex turbulence properties, properly evaluating their added value requires well-defined baseline reference models. This study establishes baseline performance thresholds for key astroclimatic parameters using two distinct models: one forecasting the parameter average over a specific timescale, and the other forecasting the temporal evolution over the same specific timescale. We apply these frameworks to extensive, multi-year datasets from the sites of the Very Large Telescope (VLT) and the Large Binocular Telescope (LBT) and discuss the possibility of extrapolating reference values of forecast performances for other sites based on their optical turbulence statistical characteristics. Our results show that baseline predictive accuracy varies according to the observing site, the specific parameter, the chosen timescale, and the forecasting approach. Therefore, an OT forecasting model's accuracy cannot be quantified in absolute terms, but relatively to the baseline.

papers.title: Multimessenger Constraints on Nuclear Acceleration in Neutrino-Emitting Seyfert Coronae
papers.abstract: High-energy neutrinos from Seyfert galaxies probe particle acceleration near supermassive black holes, but the accelerated nuclear composition remains uncertain. We connect stochastic acceleration to nuclear and radiative cascades to assess nuclear contributions. Acceleration and losses limit the energy per nucleon available to nuclear cascades; without secondary reacceleration, fragmentation cannot raise this scale. For NGC~1068, joint neutrino and gamma-ray constraints depend on the nuclear mixture: helium-dominated injection permits larger nuclear power fractions than the heavier mixtures considered. For the harder candidate {neutrino} spectrum of NGC~7469, the adopted model yields more energetic nuclear cascades, while the source-specific flux selections allow larger nuclear fractions for the heavier mixtures than in NGC~1068. These results show that composition constraints depend on nuclear yields as well as acceleration conditions and available power.

papers.title: Transient PULSE: Code for the Transient Propagation of UltraLight (pseudo)Scalars to Earth
papers.abstract: We present Transient PULSE, a software package that numerically implements a previously developed source-to-detector framework for transient ultralight bosonic signals from astrophysical bursts. Predicting these signals relies on connecting the source emission spectrum to its evolution during propagation and the resulting observables at a terrestrial detector. The package discretizes a user supplied energy spectrum into momentum modes, propagates them through a specified matter density profile and constructs the time-frequency energy density distribution at Earth, accounting for dispersion and in-medium screening effects. This treatment accommodates non-Gaussian source spectra and provides inputs for detector specific analyses. A complementary analytical module estimates coupling sensitivities, arrival time delays and screening thresholds from parameterized source and detector properties.

papers.title: International Astrophysical Consortium for High-energy Calibration: Summary of the 18th IACHEC Workshop
papers.abstract: In this report we summarize the activities of the International Astronomical Consortium for High Energy Calibration (IACHEC) from the 18th IACHEC Workshop at Pelham, Germany. Fifty-six scientists directly involved in the calibration of operational and future high-energy missions gathered during four days to discuss the status of the cross-calibration between the current international complement of X-ray observatories, and the possibilities to improve it. This summary consists of reports from the Working Groups with topics ranging across: the identification and characterization of standard calibration sources, multi-observatory cross-calibration campaigns, appropriate and new statistical techniques, calibration of instruments and characterization of background, preservation of knowledge, and results for the benefit of the astronomical community.

papers.title: GRB 181201A: Spectropolarimetric Constraints on Prompt Emission and Magnetic Field Structure
papers.abstract: Gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) have served as testbeds for high-energy astrophysical phenomena since their discovery over 50 years ago. GRB detections reveal diverse properties across events, complicating efforts to constrain their emission mechanisms, magnetic fields, jet structures, and compositions. Spectropolarimetry is a powerful tool utilized to disentangle these properties. INTEGRAL/IBIS has previously detected three polarized GRBs 041219A ($65\pm 26$%), 061122 ($>$33%) and 140206A ($>$28%). We present the time-integrated and time-resolved analyses of the fourth-polarized GRB 181201A. This GRB exhibits high polarization ($81.5^{+17.2}_{-15.7}$%) over three time bins with the highest signal-to-noise ratio, and the polarization angle (PA) shows a modest temporal evolution. The photon index does not cross the synchrotron line-of-death and shows a hard-to-soft evolution. A high degree of polarization (PD) tends to disfavor a photospheric emission model, as previous studies indicate that this model yields PD $<$ 20%. A modest evolution in the PA points towards a non-axisymmetric jet with a multi-patch emission. Our results indicate that under standard synchrotron conditions, the magnetic field is coherent but lacks global structure. Moreover, the field has multiple patches, but only one or a few dominate due to high degrees of polarization, which overlap with the intrinsic maximum of synchrotron emission within 3$σ$ errors. The high PD is also indicative of the Compton Drag scenario, but only under certain conditions, such as viewing the relativistic jet near its edge. However, given our error bars and the scope for improvement in our pipeline, we cannot strongly favor either scenario; both may remain viable.

papers.title: Refurbishment and Cryocooler Upgrade of the CPAPIR Wide-Field Near-Infrared Camera: Design, Integration, and Lessons Learned
papers.abstract: The CAmera PAnoramique Proche Infrarouge (CPAPIR) is a wide-field near-infrared imager that has been operating at the Observatoire du Mont-Mégantic (OMM) since 2004. After more than two decades of service, the instrument required a major refurbishment due to detector degradation, including the loss of one quadrant, as well as operational constraints associated with its liquid-nitrogen cooling system. To extend the instrument's lifetime and reduce maintenance requirements, the detector was replaced and the cooling system upgraded through the integration of a Sunpower CryoTel DS30 cryocooler. This paper presents the thermal and mechanical redesign of the instrument, including finite element analysis (FEA), three-dimensional CAD modeling, hardware selection, and laboratory validation. Particular attention is given to the challenges encountered during integration and testing, notably vibration mitigation and cryogenic system implementation. The resulting performance improvements and lessons learned from the upgrade are discussed. The upgraded instrument is scheduled for on-sky commissioning at the Observatoire du Mont-Mégantic in summer 2026.

papers.title: The contact frontier in Galactic civilization networks: radial structure and the Galactic habitable zone
papers.abstract: The probability of interstellar contact depends not only on the abundance of technological civilizations but also on their spatial connectivity. Treating civilizations as nodes linked whenever their separation is smaller than the distance a signal travels within a communicative lifetime, we determine the radial structure of Galactic civilization networks. An exponential stellar disc replaces the uniform disc of earlier work, and the fraction of stars hosting civilizations may vary with radius as a Galactic Habitable Zone (GHZ). The isolation, contact and network transitions are frontiers several kiloparsecs wide, not boundaries: the contact frontier is set entirely by the disc scale length, and the network frontier, broadened by gradient percolation, stays near 1.5 scale lengths. The two frontiers overlap over a band containing the Sun, where both transitions proceed at once. Within this factorized GHZ model, the radius of peak civilization density depends only logarithmically on the strength of supernova sterilization, and the wide range of published peak radii, from the Galactic centre to 12 kpc, is reproduced primarily by varying that one parameter. Under the present normalization, the location of the zone has only a modest effect on the local contact probability, whereas the modelled Galactic connectivity is minimized when the civilization-density peak lies near the solar Galactocentric radius, where current determinations place the peak.

papers.title: Updates to STIS NUV Dark Calibration
papers.abstract: We present new superdark calibration files (DARKFILEs) and a new dark correction table (TDCTAB) for use with data taken by the Space Telescope Imaging Spectrograph near-ultraviolet microchannel array (STIS NUV-MAMA) detector for HST Cycle 19 onward. These superdarks include 12 years of NUV dark exposures and make use of an updated temperature scaling equation developed in 2013 to more accurately characterize the dark rate. In tested datasets, the new superdarks provide an average 3% increase in SNR and smooth out a ring artifact left previously by oversubtraction of the dark rate. The new superdarks and TDCTAB have been delivered to the Calibration Reference Data System (CRDS) and have been used to recalibrate all affected datasets in the Mikulski Archive for Space Telescopes (MAST).

papers.title: Geometrical and Optical Design of the GUEST Laser-Ranged Test Masses for the Detection of Gravitational Waves in the $μ$Hz range
papers.abstract: The GUEST (Gravitational Universe Exploration with Satellite Tracking) mission aims at detecting gravitational waves in the yet almost unexplored $μ$Hz frequency range through high-precision orbital tracking. The unprecedented scientific objectives of this experiment demand equally advanced optical solutions: the highly eccentric orbit imposes dual measurement regimes; a low-velocity, long-range scenario at apogee and a high-velocity, short-range scenario at perigee. The substantial disparity between these conditions is addressed through a novel optical architecture incorporating two distinct types of Corner-Cube Retroreflectors (CCRs) with 1" and 2" apertures (CCR1 and CCR2, respectively). The proposed layout has been designed to ensure isotropy and homogeneity of the optical response while maintaining efficient packing over the spherical surface of the spacecraft. The resulting Optical Cross-Section (OCS) has been evaluated using a custom reduced-order model, which captures the behavior of individual CCRs under varying illumination conditions. This model has been calibrated by reconstructing the optical response of the LARES-2 satellite and has enabled a detailed assessment of the contributions of each CCR type along the GUEST orbit. Finally, sensitivity analyses have been conducted to investigate the impact of key design parameters, including the ratio between CCR types, laser wavelength, spacecraft diameter, Dihedral Angle Offsets (DAOs), and mechanical configurations.

papers.title: Revisiting the Optical F-corona from the Artemis II Total Solar Eclipse with RAW Data: How Far Can Consumer JPEG Images Be Trusted for Astronomical Photometry?
papers.abstract: We reanalyze the total solar eclipse images taken with a consumer camera during the Artemis II lunar flyby, using the RAW data as ground truth for our previous analysis of the released JPEG image. Calibrated with field stars, the RAW data show that the lens vignetting and the variation of the pixel solid angle reduce the signal of diffuse light by up to $\sim$70% at the edge of the field, and that the signal on the dark side of the Moon is most likely foreground light rather than an instrumental offset. Between 10 degrees and 15 degrees elongation, the radial profiles of the F-corona follow power laws with indices of $-2.0$ to $-2.3$ (east), $-2.5$ (west), and $-2.4$ to $-2.7$ (north and south), consistent with space-based observations, and the surface brightness along the ecliptic is $\sim$26 MJy sr$^{-1}$ ($\pm 7\%$) at 10 degrees. The isophotes have flattening indices of $\sim$0.6-0.7 and superellipse indices of $\sim$1.5-1.6. Comparison with the ZodiSURF zodiacal light model supports a radial dust density index of $α\simeq 1.3$ down to $\sim$0.2 au and suggests that the vertical distribution of the dust broadens toward the Sun. The JPEG image retains nearly the full vignetting, despite its metadata, and its tone response is not a single power law; together with the zero-point treatment, these effects account for the steep and asymmetric profiles reported previously, while the flattened morphology and $α\simeq 1.3$ are confirmed. We identify quantities robust in JPEG images and show that the tone response can be reconstructed from field stars.

papers.title: All Quiet on the Vector Front: Scalar Growth and Perturbative Control in Horndeski--Weyl-squared Gravity
papers.abstract: Higher-order curvature corrections to general relativity arise naturally in many fundamental theories and provide phenomenologically interesting low-energy effective field theories. However, higher-derivative terms can introduce ghost modes, which call the validity of such models into question. Here, we thoroughly investigate the classical linear stability of the most general second-order scalar-tensor theory, namely the Horndeski theory of gravity, augmented by a Weyl-squared term in the action. We consider shift-symmetric de Sitter and power-law FLRW backgrounds and study the evolution of linear perturbations. Vector perturbations are free of gradient and tachyonic instabilities for a positive Weyl-induced mass squared. Tensor perturbations necessarily contain a ghost; their superhorizon branches are bounded, while a frozen-background calculation identifies a separate finite-momentum stability condition. The scalar sector instead contains a growing long-wavelength branch for all expanding backgrounds we consider, which is inherited by at least one of the gauge-invariant Bardeen potentials. We show that this growth enters the Bardeen potentials through an inverse-gradient factor $a^2/k^2$: the dynamical scalar fields remain bounded on the inflationary backgrounds, the direct contribution of the growing shear to the clock-matched tidal field cancels, and the electric part of the Weyl tensor decays. We discuss the implications of our results for perturbative control and for the phenomenological viability of theories including quadratic curvature corrections.

papers.title: R&D activity in INAF on light instrumentation for continuous optical turbulence monitoring
papers.abstract: Measurements of optical turbulence are essential in both ground-based astronomy and free-space optical communication systems contexts for multiple reasons including supporting and optimizing Adaptive Optics. Similarly, forecasting these parameters is highly valuable for planning observational campaigns; however, it requires at least two years of continuous data to generate a reliable training dataset. The most commonly used instruments to monitor continuously the optical turbulence include DIMM, MASS, SLODAR, RINGSS sensors. The Arcetri team is leading two operational forecast systems for two different Observatories: ALTA above LBT, and FATE above VLT. Both systems are in continuous evolution and obviously forecast performances depend also on available measurements. Our long-term goal is to develop our own instruments to obtain continuous measurements directly from local observations. In this work, we present an automated system designed for continuous seeing measurements using multiple sensors. This portable station integrates a Cyclope, a RINGSS unit, a scintillometer which operate together to provide comprehensive night-time atmospheric information. We will compare the performance of low-cost sensors, such as the Cyclope and the scintillometer, with that of the RINGSS turbulence profiler, which has been fully installed and programmed by our team in collaboration of LBT team. A dedicated insturment for night and day-time measurements is planned for near future. This system incorporates a fully automatic on-site system that monitors operational status, delivers real-time information on sensor conditions and measurements, and manages synchronization with the data storage unit. The system's real-time acquisition capability enables continuous turbulence analysis, supports R&D activities, facilitates local data generation, and allows on-site testing of forecasting methodologies.

papers.title: Flares and flux ropes: an entangled story
papers.abstract: Solar flares serve as standard candles for all magnetic-reconnection-based energy releases, and their consequences into the heliosphere can be modeled from first principles. This review presents the latest developments in modeling solar flares and their associated flux rope expulsions with state-of-the-art multidimensional magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) descriptions. Observationally established ingredients beyond a single-fluid, thermal plasma evolution have been incorporated to varying degrees, and we highlight self-consistent efforts realized in "standard flare" setups.

papers.title: The physical and chemical structure of TMC-1. The spatial distribution and excitation conditions of carbon, oxygen, and sulfur bearing species: Depletion of CO and CS
papers.abstract: We present a detailed study of the physical and chemical structure of TMC-1 from the observed spatial distribution of HC3N, NNH+, CN, and their isotopologues, the O-bearing species C18O, C17O, CH3OH, CH3CHO, and H2CO, and the S-bearing species CS, HCS+, H2CS, and H2CCS. The well known filamentary structure of TMC-1 can be interpreted as a single cloud with a velocity gradient perpendicular to the filament, or less likely as due to the alignment of three independent clouds in the line sight with velocities of 5.3-5.7, 5.7-5.9, and 5.9-6.3 km/s. The main contribution to the emission of all studied C-bearing species is found at 5.83 kms/s. We conclude that the three velocity components are dynamically connected and that C-bearing molecules show a different behavior of their abundances compared to O-bearing species, which have emission peaks at 5.7 and 6.25 km/s, and appear at different spatial locations than cyanopolyynes and CnH and CnN radicals. The detection of 13C18O, with exactly the same line profile than that of C18O and C17O, excludes the possibility that the decrease of their emission at 5.83 km/s, could be due to self absorption or absorption by a foreground cloud component. Hence, as indicated by the spatial distribution of C18O and C17O, CO is significantly depleted at the velocities and positions where the emission of the carbon chains and radicals is found. This suggests that the emission of O-bearing species is coming from the external layers of the carbon-rich filaments. A comparison between S-bearing species and other molecules indicates that CS, CCS, HCS+, and H2CS are significantly depleted in the zone of CO depletion. A clear increase of the deuteration of several molecular species is found in the zones where CO and CS are depleted.

papers.title: Quantum noise and torque correlations in a torsion-bar Sagnac speed meter
papers.abstract: Quantum fluctuations entering through weakly transmitting mirrors can limit a torsion-bar Sagnac speed meter for low-frequency gravitational-wave detection, even when its optical layout suppresses radiation-pressure back action. We show that, in the Cryogenic sub-Hz cROss torsion bar detector with quantum NOn-demolition Speed meter (CHRONOS), vacuum fields entering from behind the end and middle test masses can dominate the low-frequency quantum noise despite cancellation of the torques on opposite ends of each bar. For a reference configuration with mirror power transmissions of only $10^{-7}$, these fields contribute $89.7\%$ of the total quantum-noise power spectral density at 0.1 Hz. Omitting them would underestimate the amplitude spectral density by a factor of 3.11. Our input-output model connects the correlations produced by successive optical interactions to the forces on each bar and the measured signal. This connection shows why strong torque cancellation does not, by itself, ensure a corresponding improvement in detector sensitivity. Replacing mirror transmission with absorption at fixed reflectivity leaves the excess quantum noise essentially unchanged for the two operating points studied. The predicted signal response and quantum noise agree with independent FINESSE 3 calculations as recycling detuning and homodyne angle are varied. These results establish rear vacuum fields as a limiting noise source in this torsion-bar speed meter and provide quantitative requirements for its mirror and readout design.

papers.title: PDRs4All XXIII. JWST-MIRI template spectra of PAHs in the Orion Bar obtained with blind signal separation
papers.abstract: The aromatic infrared bands (AIBs) are observed in a wide variety of astrophysical sources, and now in unprecedented detail by the James Webb space telescope (JWST). These bands are generally attributed to the emission from polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAHs). Our aim is to extract mid-infrared AIB template spectra from JWST observations of the Orion Bar photo-dissociation region that can be used to derive PAH properties from observations of other objects. We used the JWST MIRI-MRS observations from the PDRs4All program. We first isolated the AIBs from the data using a multi-component fitting approach. We then applied a non-negative matrix factorization to the isolated AIB spectra and extracted two templates, named AIBirrad and AIBshield following previous work. The spatial distribution and spectral characteristics of these two spectra suggest that they originate from two chemical distinct populations. We interpret AIBirrad as emission originating from a PAH population strongly exposed to ultra-violet (UV) radiation and mainly composed of large, compact ionized PAHs. Conversely, AIBshield is interpreted as originating from a more shielded population of PAHs, which is less exposed to the UV by being more embedded in the cloud. This population consists of small, asymmetric and mainly neutral PAHs with bonded aliphatic side groups. These templates can serve to analyze PAH emission in a wide variety of objects observed with MIRI-MRS.

papers.title: Linear Polarization of Synchrotron Radiation from Very-small-pitch-angle Electrons
papers.abstract: For synchrotron radiation with pitch angle $α\ll 1/γ$ where $γ$ is the electron Lorentz factor, referred to as very-small-pitch-angle synchrotron radiation, the polarization properties differ significantly from those of conventional synchrotron radiation ($α\gg 1/γ$). In this work, we investigate the linear polarization characteristics of very-small-pitch-angle synchrotron radiation from relativistic thermal and nonthermal electrons. We calculate the linear polarization by applying power-law and Maxwellian electron energy distributions. Moreover, some synchrotron sources exhibit a hybrid distribution of nonthermal and thermal electrons, and we also calculate the polarization degree for a hybrid electron energy distribution. The calculations are performed in the radio, optical, X-ray, and $γ$-ray bands. Our results show that the linear polarization degree of very-small-pitch-angle synchrotron radiation is generally lower than that of conventional synchrotron radiation. Very-small-pitch-angle synchrotron radiation from both nonthermal and thermal electrons can produce significant linear polarization. However, the polarization exhibits diverse behaviors across different physical parameters. The general scenario provided in this work can be considered for the application to all kinds of synchrotron sources, as we suggest that the very-small-pitch-angle case is crucial for the study of synchrotron polarization.

papers.title: Identifying Planetary Nebulae Candidates from IPHAS and VPHAS+ Surveys via YOLO Deep Learning Models
papers.abstract: We present a deep learning detection method capable of effectively identifying planetary nebulae (PNe) on IPHAS and VPHAS+ surveys. Our detection pipeline is based on the YOLO architecture and is adaptable to other datasets. Using the HiPS system, we preprocess and augment the $r$, $i$, and $Hα$ bands to produce two red, green, and blue (RGB) image datasets: (1) $640 \times 640$ px images at full resolution, and (2) $1 280 \times 1 280$ px images designed to capture extended objects up to $0.2$ deg. Images of $\sim 2600$ PNe are labelled using the HASH database. The loss function and evaluation metrics are adapted to the diffuse and low-contrast nature of PNe; a very low intersection over union (IoU) threshold ($1\%$) is used. A $k$-fold cross validation shows that the YOLOv12m model achieves an average precision of $0.979$ on the first dataset. At a confidence threshold of $0.15$, it achieves a precision rate of $98.7\%$ and a recall rate of $97.4\%$. We deployed our system (on $1280 \times 1280$ images) on the full surveys' coverage ($\sim 3755$ deg$^2$), and present a preliminary analysis of the detection results. The system is robust against artifacts such as CCD corner defects and HiPS tile joints. Our convolutional-neural-network-based model achieved excellent results on the test set, comparable to-or exceeding-that of a recent Swin Transformer approach. However, a challenge persists when applying deep learning models to extensive and densely populated Galactic fields: the development of an automated system that can effectively discriminate PNe from mimics that human experts are able to distinguish (e.g., H II regions). We outline possible improvements for future work.

papers.title: A possible evolutionary connection between high-mass X-ray binary pulsars and isolated rotation-powered pulsars
papers.abstract: We investigate the long-term spin evolution of high-mass X-ray binary (HMXB) pulsars in the Small Magellanic Cloud (SMC) using archival measurements of spin periods and period derivatives from XMM-Newton, Chandra, and RXTE. In the P-|dP/dt| plane, the HMXB pulsars follow an approximately linear relation in log-log space with a slope of 1.02 +/- 0.11, similar to the trend shown by the youngest isolated rotation-powered pulsars (RPPs; e.g., Manchester et al., 2005; Lorimer and Kramer, 2005). For comparison, young RPPs from the ATNF Pulsar Catalogue give slopes that depend strongly on the characteristic-age cut: 1.10 +/- 0.16 for characteristic ages below 10,000 years and 0.72 +/- 0.08 for characteristic ages below 100,000 years. The full non-recycled population shows no significant correlation. The HMXB pulsars lie in the same characteristic-age range (approximately 1,000-10,000 years) as the youngest RPPs, but at spin periods two to three orders of magnitude longer. Reference characteristic-age contours in the HMXB P-|dP/dt| plane are roughly parallel to this relation, consistent with a continuous evolutionary sequence.

papers.title: Neural networks applied to forecasting the astroclimatic and meteorological parameters in an operational context
papers.abstract: Forecasting optical turbulence and atmospheric parameters is crucial for science operations of present and new generation ground-based telescopes (ELT) as well as for free-space optical communication (FSOC). These forecasts are also useful to optimize the AO use, particularly in the ELT framework too. Recent research has demonstrated that the AR technique currently provides the best performances in predicting atmospheric and astroclimatic parameters on a time scale of 1 hour (e.g., RMSE 0.1" for the seeing), however deep learning offers some intriguing features that include the high adaptability, the correlation that can be found between different parameters treated simultaneously and different architectures can explore the capability for possible improvements. For this reason, it is important to investigate on the possibility to improve forecast performances beyond the score achieved by AR or simply to apply deep learning in those context in which it is not possible to apply the AR. In this contribution we investigate a set of algorithms belonging to the family of the neural networks that in principle are more suitable than the Random Forest (RF) model for this kind of application. We address specific questions related to the forecast performances in operational configurations. Besides that, we also investigate the impacts on gaps on the trained data set due to the lack of measurements of the optical turbulence during the day time. We show evidences that with measurements covering the whole 24-hours forecast performances might improve. Our test has been done on the wind speed in this contribution. This work is done in the framework of the operational forecast system for LBT (ALTA Center) and for the VLT (FATE project) that are leaded by our team.

papers.title: The WDM time-frequency transform in gravitational-wave data analysis II: Evolutionary spectrum and noise covariance
papers.abstract: Noise cannot be treated as stationary over the timescales required for upcoming gravitational-wave detectors, minutes for ground-based and months for space-based detectors. Nonstationarity leads to a non-diagonal frequency-domain noise covariance matrix, thus motivating a shift to the time-frequency domain. We introduce \emph{evolutionary power spectra} for describing nonstationary noise in the Wilson-Daubechies-Meyer time-frequency basis. Under the framework of oscillatory processes, we show that, to leading order in the ratio of the Meyer filter and the nonstationarity timescales, the evolutionary spectrum is a power-frequency distribution that can be estimated from a single noise realization. We derive the corresponding noise covariance matrix and show that it is band tri-diagonal, like its stationary counterpart. The exact covariance to all orders is positive semi-definite by construction and dense depending on the noise. We further derive the optimal tiling of the time-frequency plane that minimizes the error of a diagonal covariance approximation and show that coarse-graining the plane suppresses correlations quadratically. Using simulated data with a LISA Galactic foreground and a drifting powerlaw spectrum, we show that the stationarity approximation leads to signal-to-noise ratio loss and severely biases inference. For realistic LISA data, approximating the covariance as diagonal in the Wilson-Daubechies-Meyer domain is accurate for the narrow-band analysis of a single resolved Galactic binary, but insufficient for a broad-band analysis. Finally, we provide mitigation strategies for the wraparound correlations induced across the data time edges whenever the spectrum differs between the start and the end of the data.

papers.title: The convective-transition gap in 47 Tucanae with JWST
papers.abstract: We report the detection of the convective-transition gap along the lower main sequence (MS) of the Galactic globular cluster (GC) 47 Tucanae using deep James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) observations. We analyse the stellar luminosity function (LF) in the vicinity of the gap location using two independent colour-magnitude diagrams (CMDs). In both cases, the LF is characterised by a narrow gap followed by a discontinuous increase in the stellar number counts, and presents an overall morphology qualitatively consistent with that reported in previous studies. By modelling the observed LFs with an empirical likelihood model, we estimate the statistical significance of the observed feature. Additional JWST passbands exhibit similar signatures, providing further evidence for the presence of a discontinuity.

papers.title: Audible curvaton: modulated phase transition as the origin of large-scale curvature perturbations and gravitational wave anisotropies
papers.abstract: We propose a post-inflationary first-order phase transition modulated by a light spectator field as the origin of primordial large-scale curvature perturbations. Spectator fluctuations acquired during inflation modulate the bubble nucleation history, generating curvature perturbations together with correlated intrinsic gravitational-wave (GW) anisotropies. We show that this mechanism can reproduce the observed amplitude of curvature perturbations while producing a loud stochastic GW background in the frequency bands of space-based detectors such as LISA, Taiji, and TianQin. A concrete benchmark yields strongly enhanced intrinsic GW anisotropies and a local primordial non-Gaussianity signal within reach of future large-scale-structure surveys.

papers.title: Nonlinear Perturbations of Relativistic Stars
papers.abstract: We extend the general relativistic Lagrangian perturbation formalism of Friedman and Schutz [Astrophys. J. 200, 204 (1975)] beyond linear order, retaining full time dependence of the perturbations. We provide general formulae to relate the Lagrangian and Eulerian perturbations to any general perturbative order. As a proof of principle, we apply the framework to tidally perturbed relativistic stars in Regge-Wheeler gauge and reduce the second-order field and conservation equations to master equations with a nonlinear source. Projecting the source onto the star's eigenmodes, we obtain a nonlinear equation of motion for the mode amplitudes and the coupling coefficients, which describe the interactions among the eigenmodes and with the external tidal field. Approximating the tidal field and the coupling coefficients, we compute the static quadratic Love number from the quadrupolar fundamental mode alone and find that it reproduces the direct metric-matching value to a reasonable accuracy of $4\%$, up to a further correction arising from the Hamiltonian and momentum constraints of the second-order tidal field.

papers.title: Turning Selection Bias into a New Statistic: Asymmetry and Fringes of Lensed Gravitational Waves
papers.abstract: Gravitational waves (GWs) propagating across the Universe can be distorted by intervening lenses, producing characteristic wave-optics signatures. These effects are not incorporated into current matched-filtering searches and can therefore substantially reduce detection efficiency. The underlying mechanism is the signal-consistency test, which measures deviations between the observed and expected signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) distributions. We report a systematic study of the impact of gravitational lensing on signal-consistency tests, using a two-image interference model and representative signal-consistency statistics in both the time and frequency domains. We find that overlapping images produce sharply localized SNR residuals in the time domain, breaking the reflection symmetry of the autocorrelation about the merger time. Although interference fringes produce broadband SNR residuals in the frequency domain, both domains exhibit a minimum for high-mass signals when the fringe structure becomes comparable to the signal bandwidth. This highlights a limitation of current strategies that search for distorted lensed signals only among GW events detected by matched-filtering searches. Exploiting this asymmetry, we develop a statistic that separates selected down-ranked lensed injections from noise-background triggers and paired nonlensed injections, without extending the template bank. Our results establish the first connection between lensing observables and detection, paving the way for the discovery of lensed GWs.

papers.title: Reconstruction of Interstellar Cosmic Ray Anisotropy via Heliospheric Propagation Modeling and SVD Inversion
papers.abstract: Ground-based experiments such as the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the High-Altitude Water Cherenkov Gamma-Ray Observatory detect cosmic-ray anisotropy on Earth, but magnetic deflections within the heliosphere complicate interpretation. Understanding the original spatial distribution of cosmic rays in the interstellar medium requires modeling particle propagation across the heliospheric boundary. We constructed a simulated transport model that backtracks antiprotons from Earth to the interstellar medium and maps spatial transfer probabilities across energies using HEALPix representations. Because our transfer matrices are singular, inversion relies on singular value decom- position regularization. Ground-based observations lose the equatorial North-South anisotropy component, severely degrading interstellar map recovery. We developed a geometric circle-fitting algorithm to estimate and reintroduce the missing component into the observed signals. Our results show that restoring the North-South anisotropy en- ables more accurate recovery of the interstellar dipole structure. Furthermore, Poisson statistical fluctuations on the detected event counts dominate matrix-transformation errors when spread over multiple energies.
